# Add Workstation multi-window undo, redo, save, and reload

## Context

The operator goal is user-visible: multi-window actions are transactions; Workstation exposes undo/redo; saved layouts restore the same real-window composition. The manager, history, topology, effect, projection, and isolation leaves are substrate until one consumer composes them end to end.

## The Problem

Workstation currently has no undo/redo controls and its reload path can create duplicate roots or reconnect popups to an orphan. A unit test of records is insufficient: the defining behavior spans real windows, same-instance pane movement, native placement, shared Provider state, persistence, and cold/warm lifecycles.

## The Architectural Reality

Workstation is a thin consumer. Header actions bind to the Group Provider's `canUndo` / `canRedo` and dispatch manager commands; it must not keep its own stack or rescan panes. Panes remain layout-blind. App code follows the engine primitives and existing Store/Model/Provider conventions.

## Multi-window scope (operator, 2026-09-06)

**One main window with popups is this epic's multi-window story.** A user loading the same app in a second *independent* main window is a real scenario and explicitly **out of scope here**: two full roots on one App SharedWorker cannot coexist today, because the second root's `OffscreenCanvas`es are driven by a SharedWorker hosted in the first root's renderer process and Chromium terminates that process for the cross-process frame sink. That is an engine **worker-topology** question (#18376) whose fix may warrant its own epic — not a dock defect, and not something this epic's closing leaf should be gated on. A popup is unaffected because it joins its opener's process.

This narrows AC-7 below and nothing else. The cross-root isolation *implementation* shipped in #18284 and stays; only its rendered second-root receipt defers, owned by #18379, which now sits outside #18303.

## The Fix

Add Undo/Redo and save/restore affordances through existing action descriptors; wire them to the active Group; remove replaced per-window live-layout fallbacks; add one permanent multi-window Neural Link journey that exercises human and agent origins, popup movement, same-instance continuity, warm reload, and cold restore.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workstation actions | Group Provider | enabled state and commands derive from active Group | disabled with no Group/history | Workstation guide/tooltips | binding + UI arms |
| pane continuity | ADR 0029 + Neo component lifecycle | same component/controller/provider/store instances across windows | DOM rebuilt; unmodeled DOM state not promised | DockLayouts guide | identity witness |
| save/restore | topology library | save current topology; cold hydrate without replay | headless recovery on blocked popup | guide | end-to-end journey |
| popup commit target | #18284 | a gesture into this Group's own popup commits exactly once | fail closed | UI behavior docs | same-arm positive |

## Decision Record impact

Aligned with amended ADR 0029; no new ADR.

## Decision Record

Not needed beyond the prerequisite ADR amendment.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns the operator Goal and consumer proof for criteria 1, 4, 6–8, and 13. Criterion 10's rendered second-root reading is deferred with the two-independent-roots scenario (see Multi-window scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Undo/Redo actions exist once, bind to Group Provider state in main and popup windows, and dispatch no consumer-owned history logic.
- [ ] A human dock action followed by a popup move creates ordered transactions; undo/redo visibly reverses/reapplies both in cursor order.
- [ ] A Neural Link dock command interleaved with a human action shares the same cursor and reverses newest-first.
- [ ] Moving a genuinely nested pane subtree across windows preserves component, controller, Provider, and Store instance ids; new native DOM nodes mount in the target document without promising unmodeled DOM-held state.
- [ ] Warm root reload rebinds to the same Group/history and popup without replay or duplicate Workspace creation.
- [ ] Save then cold boot restores every Workspace composition plus relative popup placement; history starts empty.
- [ ] In the same production-shaped arm, Workstation A → A's own popup commits exactly once, and a repeat of the same gesture does not commit twice. **Narrowed 2026-09-06 on operator scope direction, not on implementation difficulty:** the original `A → independent Workstation B shows no preview/staging/commit` half is deferred with the two-independent-full-roots scenario (see Multi-window scope). It is not dropped — #18284 shipped the implementation with contract-level receipts, and #18379 owns the rendered receipt outside this epic, blocked by #18376.
- [ ] Single-window/history-disabled Workstation behavior loads no history module and remains functional.
- [ ] Replaced per-window live-layout persistence and sync sweeps are deleted, with an explicit deletion ledger.

## Out of Scope

New transaction semantics, cross-Group bridging, pane-specific persistence, styling unrelated to the controls, and the two-independent-full-roots scenario with its worker-topology fix (#18376).

## Avoided Traps

No app-local stack; no presentation sweep; no DOM-identity claim; no fixture-only multi-window host; no happy-path-only restore; no duplicate implementation of manager rules. Added 2026-09-06: no rendered receipt manufactured from a modified product configuration to satisfy a scenario the epic does not cover.

## Related

Part of #18303. Final consumer leaf; blocked by every semantic/persistence/projection prerequisite. Related D#18150 for Workspace façade deletion. #18379 carries the deferred second-root receipt outside this epic.

- 2026-09-06T10:28:31Z @neo-opus-ada cross-referenced by PR #18381
- 2026-09-06T10:41:51Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `4c1692e` - "test(dock): a history-disabled Group answers the chain without loading the history module (#18316)

The manager's default depth is zero, so a single-window app has no history at
all. Reading the Group's state must not be what drags the module into that app's
closure: `historyState` reads through `history?.`, so an absent history answers
`false` rather than becoming a reason to load one.

The arm asserts the load count immediately after the only call that could
trigger it. Positive control run: with the Group's depth raised to five the same
write records three loads and the assertion fails on its own message, so the
probe can produce the falsifying result rather than merely matching the shape it
was written to expect."
- 2026-09-06T10:43:54Z @neo-gpt-emmy cross-referenced by PR #18382
- 2026-09-06T10:48:38Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `fa62f80` - "feat(workstation): the app declares a history depth, which is what makes Undo reachable (#18316)

A Group is born at depth zero: it keeps no history and loads no history module
until a consumer asks for one. Nothing in the product ever asked. Undo and Redo
were therefore correctly bound to `canUndo` / `canRedo` and permanently
disabled — a control that can never enable, which reads as shipped.

Workstation is the consumer that puts those controls on screen, so it declares
the depth for its own Group rather than taking a worker-wide default that would
reach every other root in the same worker. The declaration sits in
`afterSetTopologyGroupId` because that hook runs when the Group is learned,
which is before that Group's first write — the point the manager's contract
requires.

The number is not invented: D#18224 measured this exact document at depth 50 and
found 1.04x latency against a collection.Base baseline, so it is a bound we have
evidence is affordable here. The JSDoc carries that reasoning without the
tracking ref, which the archaeology guard correctly refused.

The arm carries its own control: it asserts the manager default is zero, so the
reader can see what the declaration prevents rather than taking the claim on
trust."
- 2026-09-06T11:20:33Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `0e06308` - "feat(dock): undo and redo read the Group's history through the provider chain (#18316)

A dock workspace parents its own state provider to its Group's, so `canUndo`,
`canRedo`, `historyCursor`, `historyDepth` and `historyLength` reach any bound
component beneath it — in whichever window that component renders, because a
window is a render target and not a state owner.

Workstation's topology bar is the first consumer: Undo and Redo are action
descriptors whose `disabled` is a binding onto those leaves and whose handlers
are a bare manager dispatch. The consumer keeps no stack, mirrors no cursor and
re-derives nothing per commit.

Install and teardown come from the same manager instance. The link is created off
whichever manager answered — including the global one a host reaches without ever
triggering the tear-out opt-in's dynamic load — so the retirement listener is
registered there too; otherwise a host that never opted in would keep a destroyed
provider answering in its chain after `retireGroup`. The arm that proves this
found it."

- 2026-09-06T11:20:33Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `c3ceca4` - "fix(dock): a sibling projection no longer discards the panes the commit parked (#18316)

Sibling convergence hands each owner's `project` callback the item ids owned by
the other documents in the committed snapshot, and the host passes them into
`projectDockZoneDocument`. That spread let the caller's list REPLACE the one
`getRefreshOptions` derives from the descriptor — but a consumer's override
lifts a commit-scoped park off that descriptor, and both lists name panes that
must outlive the projection. Whichever lost was destroyed.

`preserveItemIds` is now the union of the two. Every other option stays
last-writer-wins, because only the id set is additive: the reconciler already
treats it that way where it merges the same field again downstream. The result
is absent rather than empty when neither side names an id, matching the shape
`getRefreshOptions` emits.

Not reachable on the current tree — `set.write` has exactly one caller and it
hardcodes a descriptor with no park — so this lands ahead of the producers
rather than after a failure. It arms as soon as a Group writer carries a park on
this callback, which the remaining epic leaves add.

Red-first control: with the union reverted to the plain spread, the arm loses
the parked id and fails; restored, both arms pass. Dashboard and Workstation
trees 955 passed, 0 failed."

- 2026-09-06T12:11:23Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `fd563a8` - "test(workstation): a cold boot's empty log is read through the control that binds it (#18316)

`expectColdTopology` already asserted the empty log from the manager's projected
state. This reads the same fact from the other end: `stateProvider.getData`,
which is what the topology bar's Undo binds to. Together they say the affordance
a user meets is disabled, not merely that the manager knows it should be.

The depth assertion is what makes the rest mean anything. The app now declares a
real history depth, so an empty log after a cold boot is a Group that COULD hold
history and does not — rather than one that never had the capacity, which is all
the assertion could have shown before.

Control: with the cold hydrate's cursor switched from preserve to append, the arm
reds on the pre-existing empty-history assertion; restored, 1/1 passes in 25.2s
against a real Chrome cold boot over the Neural Link."

- 2026-09-06T19:07:34Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `163dd45` - "fix(dock): a Group link displaces a configured parent only for the Group's lifetime (#18316)

Emmy's RA-1. Binding a valid Group replaced whatever parent a consumer had
configured on the workspace's own provider, and retirement then set it to null
rather than putting it back — so a consumer's ancestry did not survive a Group
it never asked to join.

The parent standing at install time is now captured before the first link and
restored when the Group retires. Captured once rather than per re-point: a
workspace learning a second Group would otherwise record the FIRST Group's
provider as the thing to restore and hand the consumer a chain it never
configured.

The claim is corrected rather than widened. A provider has one parent and the
Group's is shared by every workspace in that Group, so its ancestry cannot be
re-pointed at one consumer's chain without deciding it for all of them. What the
seam guarantees is a BOUNDED displacement, and the JSDoc now says that instead
of implying preservation throughout.

My previous arm only covered the unresolvable-Group path, where nothing is
installed and nothing can be clobbered — a control over the null case. The new
arm reads consumer data before attachment, asserts the Group's leaves answer
while bound, and asserts the configured parent returns after retirement.
Control run: reverting the restore to `null` fails it on its own message."
- 2026-09-06T19:19:14Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `97ffae0` - "fix(dock): Group history is a projection, so consumer ancestry is never touched (#18316)

Emmy's RA-1, held open correctly. Restoring the parent at retirement returned it
only once it no longer mattered: enabling docking history cannot cost a consumer
the stores and application data it inherits for the whole running lifetime. That
was the original defect made deliberate, not fixed.

The provider chain is now left entirely alone. The Group's five leaves are
published onto the workspace's own provider under `dockHistory`, the way
HeaderActionPolicy publishes header truth — one source, a projection at the
commit boundary, and self-diffing leaves so an unchanged republish moves nothing.
The manager's own `commit` signal carries it, scoped by groupId.

This keeps both properties the RA named: consumer ancestry intact BEFORE, WHILE
and AFTER a Group is bound, and shared Group ownership untouched, since nothing
re-parents a provider that many workspaces read.

Retirement publishes the empty shape rather than deleting the namespace, so a
bound `disabled` formatter reads a real `false` instead of `undefined` at exactly
the moment its Group goes away.

The arm now reads consumer data at all three points. Unit trees 980 passed."

- 2026-09-06T19:35:32Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `616e67b` - "refactor(workstation): Undo and Redo read the Group's leaf where it lives (#18316)

Emmy's guidance on the RA-1 completion, and it removes code rather than adding
it. The projection layer is gone: `state.Provider#getData` resolves to the leaf's
own `core.Config`, so a formatter reading the Group's provider inside a binding
effect registers that exact leaf and re-runs when it changes. Direct reactive
reads already worked; a mirror was never needed.

publishes provider state directly without firing `commit`, so a commit-fed copy
would have gone stale exactly there — a second publication path that had to be
kept in step with the first. There is now one path.

touches `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` not at all — the whole delivery is the
app binding to state the engine already publishes.

The AC-2 arm also stops counting rows and names the one it witnesses. Counting
made it a settle race against the pop-out's own rows: it failed once at 31.7s and
passed at 4.2s on re-run with no code change. `native-popup-move` has exactly one
producer, so its presence is the witness. 3/3 runs at ~3.9s; the suppressed-move
control still fails on its own message.
